members.obligation: Per-window Stale/Unsupported pacing observation states and hard-hold creation evidence (PRX-QUAL-003, PRX-QUAL-004)
acceptanceCriteria: WindowStatus has Observed, Missing, Invalid, Stale and Unsupported, each with a stable code in status JSON coverage.

A window carried from a cached reading (not in the current response) is Stale, never Observed; a window kind the adapter does not support (unknown Claude limit kind, unknown Codex slot) is Unsupported with a diagnostic, never silently dropped.
Stale and Unsupported expected windows make the reading incomplete (freshness stale), with response-shape drift reported as an explicit diagnostic.

Hard-limit holds persist creation evidence (observedAt of the triggering reading and the provider window reference) in hold.json as an additive schema-2 field that older readers ignore; holds without it read as unrecorded, never invented.
Tests cover each state and the migration.

members.obligation: Typed provider, model, quota-bucket and scope identities for pacing (PRX-QUAL-005)
acceptanceCriteria: ProviderId, ModelId and QuotaBucket are typed values at the Application/Domain boundary; QuotaScope matching uses typed model-family identity with no String.Contains substring matching in policy.
Codex Spark bucket selection and Claude scope mapping are explicit, versioned adapter rules (one table each) with fixtures.
Unknown models have a declared conservative behaviour: every scoped window applies.
Adapter id, rule-set version and capabilities are observable in pacing status (text and JSON).
An architecture/guard test refuses Contains-based model matching in the pacing domain and application.

members.obligation: Typed pacing telemetry events with stable codes replacing free-text pace.log (PRX-QUAL-008)
acceptanceCriteria: The gate emits typed PacingEvent values with stable codes: hold-started, hold-retained, hold-released, hard-limit, provider-unavailable, override-enabled, override-disabled, state-fault.
Events carry provider, scope, reason kind, reset time and observedAt, never credentials, tokens or raw provider payloads.
Repeated polling with an unchanged hold emits no duplicate transition events (deduplicated by transition identity).
Events persist as praxis.pacing-event/1 JSON lines (events.jsonl) and pace.log remains as a human-readable rendering of the same events; readers (docs, status) are migrated.
Tests cover codes, redaction and deduplication.

members.obligation: Adversarial pacing adapter tests: Keychain, HTTP errors and redirects, provider process timeout/EOF, live hook fixtures (PRX-QUAL-011)
acceptanceCriteria: Claude credential decoding is testable without a real Keychain: Keychain unavailable, missing entry, expired credential and malformed credential are explicit errors and the snapshot is unavailable, never fresh.
The Claude usage query is testable through an injected HTTP handler: a 3xx redirect is refused without following it, 4xx/5xx are explicit errors.
The provider process protocol is testable with a scripted stand-in: timeout, EOF before reply, error reply and malformed JSON are explicit errors.
Recorded live hook payload fixtures for Claude Code and Codex (PreToolUse and Stop events) drive the gate end to end and produce the provider's documented deny shape.
No test uses the live network or a real credential store.
